summary: John White's proposal for a Network Mail Protocol, a far richer replacement for the two FTP mail commands MAIL and MLFL. It is explicitly a request for comments rather than a final specification, and invites bug reports and position papers.

plainLanguage.summary: A plan for a full set of rules for sending letters between computers, going beyond the simple tools used until then.

questions: what are the mp mail functions
subtitle: John White's 1973 proposal for a mail protocol that lives inside FTP and goes far beyond the MAIL and MLFL commands.

tldr.problem: Network mail was handled by two FTP commands, MAIL and MLFL, which could only hand a file or string of text to a server as mail for a local user. They lacked recording, forwarding, acknowledgments and verified authorship.
tldr.mechanism: The Mail Protocol (MP) is a subsystem of FTP entered with the MAIL command. It defines seven functions: recording, delivery, distribution, forwarding, citation retrieval, citation update and user verification.
tldr.outcome: The RFC says plainly that it is a Request for Comments with bugs to be found. It invites comments, questions and position papers.

today: The unit metadata lists the status of RFC 524 as Unknown, and it is not marked as obsoleted or updated. The RFC itself calls the document a proposal and a request for comments.

sections.title: MP as a Subsystem of FTP
sections.content:
John White of SRI-ARC writes that mail was then handled by two FTP commands, MAIL and MLFL. The proposed protocol is much richer in both function and flexibility. The author invites readers to report bugs through the RFC series.

MP is implemented by Mail user and server processes that are also FTP user and server processes. Its commands are a subsystem entered from the FTP command space with MAIL and left only with EXIT. Inside it, MP commands are accepted and FTP commands are rejected, and the same name can mean different things in each space. A note suggests XMAIL as a name while the old mail commands are phased out.

MP follows FTP syntax: NVT characters, command names of four or fewer alphameric characters, lines ending with CR LF, and replies with a numeric and a text part. It uses reply codes whose second digit is 7 for its own results. The subsystem idea comes from Mike Padlipsky's Unified User Level Protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: MP is a special room inside the FTP building. You enter with MAIL, follow the room's own rules, and leave with EXIT.

sections.title: The Mail Model and Its Roles
sections.content:
MP defines mail as text communicated between users, human or process, in less than (but ideally approaching) real time. Console-to-console exchange is excluded. Mail can be forwarded, replied to, authenticated to avoid forgery, and permanently recorded under a long-term identifier and entered in catalogs, with access restricted to chosen people.

The glossary defines the roles. A Clerk prepares a piece of mail. A Delivery Agent transmits it to a recipient's host. A Distribution Agent accepts mail for other hosts and takes responsibility for delivering it and acknowledging back to the Monitor. A Recording Agent stores a Citation permanently and assigns a pathname. Recorded mail has static attributes (Content, Title, Comments, Authors, Clerk, Creation Date) that never change, and dynamic attributes (Distribution, Access and Catalog Lists) that holders of Controlling Access can modify.

Each delivery has a status: SUCCESSFUL, FAILED, WAITING, TIMED OUT or UNATTEMPTED. An acknowledgment condition of ALWAYS, FAILURE or NEVER says when to report, with FAILURE as the default. The default cutoff interval, after which delivery attempts are abandoned, is 7 days.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail here can be a quick note or an official document. Some computers act as post offices that keep trying to deliver and then send back a receipt, and others act as archives that keep a copy forever.

sections.title: The Seven Functions
sections.content:
A host may implement any, all or none of the functions. If it implements none, it replies 400 Function not implemented.; if it wants a login first, it replies 332 Login first, please. The reply to MAIL lists the supported functions (code 271). Each function is opened by a command and ended by EXIT to carry it out or ABORT to do nothing.

  • RECORD: store mail permanently. Content and Clerk are required, and the server returns a pathname (code 270).
  • DELIVER: send mail to recipients. Content and a Distribution List are required.
  • DISTRIBUTE: hand mail to a Distribution Agent, with optional acknowledgment, cutoff and progress report settings.
  • FORWARD: pass unread mail to another individual.
  • RETRIEVE: get selected parts of a record's Citation by pathname; the components come back as reply 172 lines and end with 173.
  • UPDATE: change dynamic attributes, with the requestor checked for Controlling Access.
  • VERIFY: check an ID; reply 272 if correct, 472 if not.

Content is sent either as a file, with the FTP data transfer commands, or inline as lines with TEXT. MP also borrows FTP commands such as USER, PASS, ACCT, HELP and NOOP.
sections.plainLanguage: There are seven jobs the mail room can do, like filing a copy, mailing a letter, forwarding it, looking up a filed one, changing who may read it, and checking who someone is. Each job starts with a command and ends by saying go ahead or never mind.

sections.title: A Recorded and Distributed Message
sections.content:
The RFC's worked example records a short public message about SMFS on TENEX 1.31 at the NIC and then distributes it to one recipient. This is described as the implementation of NIC Journal Submission, with the NIC acting as both Recording and Distribution Agent.

After RECORD and EXIT, the server returns the pathname 15490. The distribution then names that message by location, adds a recipient, greeting and signature, asks for an acknowledgment whether delivery succeeds or fails, asks for it to be terse, and sets a cutoff of one day.
sections.plainLanguage: The example is like filing a note in the archive, getting a shelf number back, and then asking the post office to deliver that filed note to one person and report back.

viz.caption: OPENING LINES OF THE RFC 524 EXAMPLE

data.title: Entering MP and recording a message
data.code:
MAIL <CA>
   [261 RE DE DI FW CI UP UV -- supported.]
REC <CA>
   [200 OK.]
TITL SMFS Runs on TENEX 1.31 at the NIC <CA>
   [200 OK.]
EXIT <CA>
   [270 15490 -- is assigned as the pathname.]
